events.title: Apache Kafka open-sourced
events.summary: LinkedIn open-sourced [Kafka] on January 11, 2011 — a distributed, persistent log for high-throughput event streaming.
events.about: [Kafka] appends events to partitioned topics that many consumers read at their own pace — ideal for activity tracking, log aggregation, and stream processing. It became the backbone of real-time data pipelines at LinkedIn, Uber, and Netflix before managed cloud offerings. Example: clickstream events land in a `pageviews` topic; analytics and recommendation jobs consume them independently.

narrative.whyChosen: [Kafka] open-sourced LinkedIn's solution for billions of daily activity events.
narrative.whyImportant: It defined the modern event-streaming architecture that powers analytics and microservice decoupling.
narrative.problemSolved: Traditional message queues could not retain and replay massive event histories at log scale.

events.title: Kohsuke Kawaguchi renames Hudson to Jenkins
events.summary: Kohsuke Kawaguchi led the [Hudson] community to rename the project Jenkins on January 11, 2011 — breaking from Oracle's trademark control after the [Sun] [acquisition].
events.about: The [Hudson]→Jenkins fork preserved the world's most widely used CI server as community-governed software. Jenkins became the default build [automation] tool in [Java] shops and later across polyglot pipelines.

narrative.whyChosen: The Jenkins rename was a landmark open-source governance fight with Oracle.
narrative.whyImportant: It kept continuous integration tooling under community control when trademark disputes threatened the project.
narrative.problemSolved: Oracle's [Hudson] trademark claims put the project's name and infrastructure at corporate risk.

events.title: Drupal 7 released
events.summary: [Drupal] 7.0 shipped on January 5, 2011 — a major usability and fields overhaul that powered government and enterprise sites for a decade.
events.about: [Drupal] 7 added Fields in core, better image handling, and a refined admin [UI] — the version most large [Drupal] shops ran until [Drupal] 8/9 migrations. It paired with Views, Pathauto, and Commerce modules for complex content architectures.

narrative.whyChosen: [Drupal] 7 was the stable peak of classic [Drupal] before the [Symfony] rewrite.
narrative.whyImportant: Fields [API] and UX improvements made [Drupal] viable for large institutional deployments.
narrative.problemSolved: [Drupal] 6 required contrib modules for basic content modeling that sites expected in core.
